//: A TRIPWIRE, NOT A TARGET. A run covering LESS than this fails prun, because every shard that ran will have passed and nothing else would say so. Raise it when the suite grows; LOWER it in the same commit that removes assertions, so the reduction is a decision on the record rather than a number that quietly followed the code down.
//why-recorded: Deliberately NOT derived from the suite. An expectation computed by the same scan that finds the sections is satisfied by finding none of them — which is how a run that dispatched nothing prints a plausible small green total. The floor has to come from outside the run.
//measured-by: python3 test/prun.py — the distinct count it prints, and the section group count.
//machine-dependence: THE FLOOR IS WHAT A FRESH CLONE COVERS, not what this checkout does. Two assertions in 'every configured trigger command actually exists' are derived from .game_loop/triggers.json, which is GITIGNORED — a clone legitimately has none, and that section skips honestly rather than failing. Measured each time, in a clone, never subtracted: this checkout 2052, a `git clone` of it 2050. Recording 2034 made every consumer's run report SUITE FLOOR BREACHED for a documented skip, which is the one thing a tripwire must never do: cry loss where nothing was lost. A floor above the minimum any legitimate checkout reaches is not a tripwire, it is a false alarm with a number on it.
